### IL-247: Hard rule — No smart refactor without repo-wide duplication verification (Duplication Audit) — ADR-102 [Governance]
- **Date:** 2026-06-16
- **Repos:** banxe-architecture only (this PR — ADR-102 + AGENTS.md + .claude/rules/agents.md + ledger). No code repo or trading-platform prod repo touched.
- **Numbering:** next free after IL-246 is IL-247 (the IL-2027 and IL-2028 headings are the typo numbers canonized by the IL-235 errata as IL-228 and IL-229; the real high-water mark is IL-246). Append-only, no existing IL edited.
- **What:** Add a hard STOP-barrier rule for Claude Code and MetaClaw/OpenClaw and every code-changing agent: No smart refactor without repo-wide duplication verification. Before any structural change (restructuring, moving modules, deleting code, deduplication) the agent MUST complete a mandatory five-step Duplication Audit and record it in the task or ADR artefact, and no structural change merges without it. The five steps: (1) repo-wide semantic and textual search for duplicate implementations, interfaces, DTOs, helpers, SQL, migration fragments and docs across all in-scope repos; (2) identify the source-of-truth and every consumer of each duplicate; (3) no delete or merge until the absence of hidden dependencies is positively confirmed; (4) attach a Duplication Audit section with matches found, decision per match (keep or merge or delete) and risks; (5) if in doubt, fail-closed and escalate to a human. A refactor PR without a Duplication Audit section is incomplete and is rejected.
- **ADR:** new ADR-102 (Status ACCEPTED) — the hard rule plus the five-step protocol, at invariant priority (alongside the no-skip-flags and fail-closed barriers), above local agent discretion. Motivated by the legacy migration track (large duplicated legacy bases).
- **Docs:** AGENTS.md (developer-core canon) gains a HARD RULE section with the five-step summary and a pointer to ADR-102; .claude/rules/agents.md gains the rule as a STOP-barrier with the full protocol.
- **Surface:** governance docs only; no code, no endpoint, no /v1 change.
- **Proof:** arch required checks ADR Validation, Secrets Scan, ledger-append-only, guardian-* (incl. guardian-ledger coupling and branch-naming) plus Markdown Link Check and Mermaid and CodeRabbit green; INSTRUCTION-LEDGER.md append-only (only IL-247 added); branch follows the ADR-060 agent/factory namespace.
- **Canon:** docs-first, ADR-governed (ADR-102), append-only ledger (I-28, ADR-056). No protection toggled, no visibility change, no repo created.
- **OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED:** none — this is a self-imposed factory hard rule; it tightens, never loosens, the refactor discipline.
- **Refs:** ADR-102, ADR-056 (ledger-coupling); AGENTS.md; .claude/rules/agents.md.

### IL-248: Server-only refactoring & smart-refactor promotion gate — ADR-103 [Governance]
- **Date:** 2026-06-16
- **Repos:** banxe-architecture only (this PR — ADR-103 + ledger). Docs-only; no code, no infra, no trading-platform prod repo touched. PR opened, NOT merged.
- **Numbering:** next free after IL-247 is IL-248 (the IL-2027 and IL-2028 headings are the typo numbers canonized by the IL-235 errata as IL-228 and IL-229; the real high-water mark is IL-247). Append-only, no existing IL edited.
- **What:** Establish a two-part security policy. PART 1 (server-only refactoring): all refactoring and legacy-code handling (archive unpacking, snapshotting, inventory and mapping M0 through Mn, analysis, and any factory code edits), factory repo cloning and edits, and secret use run ONLY on a secured server (for example evo1 or a dedicated runner), never on an operator local machine. The operator local machine is a thin client (gh or ssh) with no local storage of legacy sources or repo working copies and no secrets; hard prohibition on unpacking or processing legacy archives and on refactoring git-operations in the local OS /tmp, and on entering secret values into a local shell; secrets live server-side only (server vault or GitHub Actions secrets). PART 2 (smart-refactor promotion gate): moving a result into a target repository happens only after the server-side refactoring completes and only via the smart-refactor discipline, i.e. a mandatory repo-wide Duplication Audit (ADR-102) on the promotion PR (repo-wide search, source-of-truth plus every consumer, no delete or merge until hidden dependencies are ruled out, a Duplication Audit section with keep or merge or delete plus risks, fail-closed and escalate on doubt). A promotion PR is rejected if its result was not produced by the server-side refactor or if it lacks the completed Duplication Audit.
- **Canonical pipeline:** server workspace setup; legacy ingest to the server (no local /mnt/c); server-side refactor M0 through Mn; Duplication Audit (ADR-102); promotion PR into the target repo; review and merge via the protected-main flow. The local machine only initiates via gh or ssh; every step executes on the server.
- **Docs/rules updated:** AGENTS.md and .claude/rules/agents.md each gain a HARD RULE block "Refactoring runs server-only; promotion only via smart refactor (Duplication Audit)" pointing to ADR-103.
- **Current-state GAP (pre-policy debt):** M0 (archive unpack plus /tmp/bx-legacy snapshot plus /tmp/bx-legacy-tools utilities plus BANXE_RAR_PASSWORD in the local shell on mark-legion) and Fix A and Fix B for banxe-emi-stack PR #36 (clone to /tmp/emi-fix plus pushes from the local environment) were performed locally before this policy. They are flagged as pre-policy debt to be re-homed to the server contour; the analysis is valid, only the execution location is non-compliant and must migrate.
- **Migration outline (non-binding; concretised later):** a secured server hosts the refactor and legacy workspace (for example /srv/banxe-legacy), access-controlled and audited; BANXE.RAR reaches the server without a local /mnt/c step (direct upload or server-side pull, manifest checksums verified there); the factory drives work via ssh or a self-hosted runner job (clone, edit, push server-side); secrets live in a server vault or GitHub Actions secrets and are injected at runtime, never typed into a local shell.
- **ADR:** new ADR-103 (Status ACCEPTED) — server-only refactoring and smart-refactor promotion gate, two STOP-barriers (PART 1 execution location, PART 2 promotion gate) for the factory agents, explicitly invoking ADR-102 as the mandatory promotion step.
- **Duplication Audit (ADR-102):** searched docs/adr, .claude/rules, AGENTS.md, docs/canon for an existing execution-location or server-only or thin-client policy AND for an existing promotion-gate policy. No duplicate of either. ADR-040 governs meta versus inference plane model routing, ADR-051 governs which coder (Claude versus local), ADR-047 governs cost tiers (matched the word promotion but not refactor-result promotion), and ADR-102 is the Duplication-Audit rule this gate invokes rather than duplicates; none defines the physical execution location of refactoring nor a promotion gate for moving refactor results into repos. Verdict keep (new policy), no merge or supersede, risk none.
- **Surface:** governance docs only; no code, no endpoint, no /v1 change, no infra.
- **Proof:** arch required checks ADR Validation, Secrets Scan, ledger-append-only, guardian-* (incl. guardian-ledger coupling and branch-naming), Markdown Link Check, Mermaid and CodeRabbit expected green; INSTRUCTION-LEDGER.md append-only (only IL-248 added); branch follows the ADR-060 agent/factory namespace. PR opened, merge NOT performed.
- **Canon:** docs-first, ADR-governed (ADR-103), append-only ledger (I-28, ADR-056), compliance-first (security policy reducing local attack surface). No protection toggled, no visibility change, no repo created.
- **OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED:** standing up the server workspace and ingress path (a follow-up infra sprint) and migrating the M0 and Fix A/B pre-policy debt to the server. This ADR sets the policy; the infra realization is a separate gated step.
- **Refs:** ADR-103, ADR-040 (AI execution plane), ADR-051 (coding execution decision), ADR-047 (cost governance), ADR-102 (refactor duplication discipline); AGENTS.md and .claude/rules/agents.md (hard-rule mirror); current-state GAP M0 + banxe-emi-stack PR #36 Fix A/B.

### ADR-060 pre-push gate — root-cause bug fix (STDIN refs) + deterministic test; evo1/evo2 ACTIVATED
- **Bug (found on evo2 self-test):** branch with hyphen in <id> `agent/factory/archstack-subA/x` was NOT blocked locally, though ADR-060 requires block. Legion gave BLOCKED — divergence.
- **Root cause:** scripts/pre-push-branch-name.sh read `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` instead of the refs git hands the pre-push hook on STDIN (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>`). `git push origin <bad-branch>` while HEAD sat on `main` validated `main` (allow-listed) → bad branch passed. Legion happened to have HEAD == the test branch, masking the bug. Regex itself is correct + byte-for-byte identical to guardian.yml.
- **Fix (scripts/pre-push-branch-name.sh):** read EACH pushed ref from STDIN, normalize refs/heads/ prefix, validate via a pure shared validator is_compliant(); manual/empty-STDIN fallback to current branch; detached-HEAD safe. Deterministic across hosts.
- **Test added (scripts/test-branch-name-gate.sh):** 15-case PASS/BLOCK table sourcing is_compliant() — no git-state dependence → Legion/evo1/evo2/CI identical. Result: ALL CASES GREEN (15/15); STDIN-contract sim blocks hyphen-id regardless of HEAD.
- **Terminal status:** evo1 + evo2 hooks **ACTIVATED** (replaces the prior false DEFERRED). evo2: HTTPS read-clone OK (HEAD e6bbe6b), install-hooks OK, host-key fingerprint SHA256:Jtjc…ABk; self-test surfaced+fixed this bug. Legion: ALL CASES GREEN.
- **Pending follow-up (tracked):** deploy-key for **push from evo2** (currently read-only HTTPS; push needs 2FA Confirm-access / deploy-key) — separate enablement step.
- **Proof:** build_ledger --check OK; validate_schemas PASS; del=0; org-docs (DEPARTMENT-MAP/ROADMAP/HITL-MATRIX) NOT touched; no service code (gate script + test harness + ledger only).

### Canon Fast-Lane Simplification — risk-tiered lane model + operator policy changes to accelerate BANXE smart-refactor migration (docs-only)
- **Referer:** Canon fast-lane simplification for BANXE smart refactor migration. Governance proposal; DOCS-ONLY; NO code/runtime/migration-branch mutation; NO KYC touch; NO merge.
- **Instrukciya:** Analyze what unjustifiably blocks migration throughput and propose a best-decision canon that removes ceremony from low-risk work WITHOUT weakening safety guardrails.
- **Unjustified frictions identified (evidence-based):** (1) excessive IL/ledger churn on descriptive/additive docs; (2) il_ts collision management as constant overhead (readiness re-mint 13:30→13:45→14:00; "Sisyphus loop" per LEDGER-MERGE-QUEUE.md); (3) stale CONFLICTING/forced-nudge cases (main moved 8+/window); (4) docs-only PR batch-merge overhead; (5) over-fragmentation into micro-steps where one governance step blocks the next useful additive scaffold; (6) operator-gated mode over-applied to low-risk descriptive/additive surfaces; (7) one-size-fits-all heavy process for high- AND low-risk actions.
- **Proposed canon (3 lanes):** 🟢 Fast (docs-only, low-risk scaffolds, descriptive/additive ports, adapter shells, roster/coverage updates) · 🟡 Controlled (bounded-context code migration, no live-state touch) · 🔴 Strict (KYC/KYB/AML, auth-crypto runtime, token/session issuance, live balances/ledger mutations, production cutover). Fail-safe: ambiguous → stricter lane.
- **Fast-lane simplifications:** batch docs/IL updates in one PR; no separate governance-merge cycle without code/runtime risk; replace per-PR il_ts arbitration with deterministic batch-window OR merge-time sequencer; one-PR-per-sprint for related low-risk artifacts; no governance stop between consecutive low-risk scaffolds.
- **Controlled-lane:** keep worktree/branch isolation + CI + ADR-102 on delete/merge + ADR-103 server-side; trim to one IL shard per BC + two operator checkpoints (plan, promotion).
- **Operator policy changes (P1-P6):** P1 sprint-batch docs+IL PRs; P2 merge-time il_ts allocation / monotonic auto-sequencer; P3 one-PR-per-sprint low-risk; P4 remove governance stop between consecutive low-risk scaffolds; P5 mandatory operator approval ONLY for strict-lane; P6 enable GitHub merge queue (operator-privileged, runbook already on main).
- **What stays STRICT (no dilution):** KYC/KYB/AML, SRP runtime activation, token/session issuance, live balances/ledger mutations, production cutover/re-point.
- **Effective operating model:** sprint-based execution; one best-next-action artifact; batch low-risk work; fewer governance interrupts; direct progress to 100% migration of relevant microservices.
- **Safety:** no invariant (I-21..I-28) weakened; append-only ledger + ADR-102/103 intact; throughput gain = removing ceremony, not controls; misclassification errs toward MORE control.
- **Coupling/append-only:** branch agent/factory/canonfastlane/fast-lane-simplification (off main); new tail shard → IL-456 after final-rebase onto main@b2bde95; no prior entry mutated; il_ts 15:15:00Z strictly > re-fetched main max 15:05:00Z (#696 M1.26 changelog-spec took 15:05Z; our 15:15Z slot stayed free → no bump needed this pass). Earlier churn-loop passes: 14:30→15:15 after #699 MIG-TEMPLATE merged — a live instance of friction #2/#3 this very proposal targets.
- **Proof:** docs+ledger only; build_ledger.py --check exit 0; guardian-ledger/ledger-append-only/guardian-ledger-shards/guardian-branch-naming/guardian-adr117 green locally; force-with-lease push; NO --admin/bypass; docs-only PR opened, NO merge.

- **Decision (ADR-119):** заморозить IL-NNN per shard в append-only ledger/IL-SEQUENCE.json (key=<session_id>__<hex>, hex=sha1(path)[:12], collision-proof). (1) init once реплеем legacy (il_ts,session_id,path)+FROZEN-offset нумерации → каждый существующий shard сохраняет ТОЧНО свой номер; (2) known shards reuse frozen number; (3) new shards = max+1 в (il_ts,session_id,path) order, APPEND в IL-SEQUENCE.json (existing keys/values никогда не мутируются/удаляются); (4) ledger рендерится в IL-number order → новая запись всегда tail независимо от il_ts → behind-PR не renumber-ит и не требует re-mint.
- **Proof:** build_ledger.py modified (load/assign/render/dump_sequence/head_sequence/check_append_only); ledger/IL-SEQUENCE.json NEW (208 keys, IL-249..456 contiguous; origin/main 232e846 incl canon-fast-lane IL-456 #701). Behavior-preserving: регенерированный INSTRUCTION-LEDGER.md BYTE-IDENTICAL к origin/main (0 deletions, 0 renumber). Regression (in-memory, no file writes): probe shard early il_ts 2026-06-01 → assigned max+1 (tail), rendered LAST, 0 prior keys shifted = PASS. build_ledger.py --check OK (ledger sync + IL-SEQUENCE sync + append-only vs git HEAD). guardian-ledger coupling satisfied этим shard (ADR-119 IL block appended at tail = IL-457). Invariants preserved: I-28/append-only (shards + IL-SEQUENCE.json self-checked; ledger deletions rejected), ADR-056 ledger-coupling + ADR-059 sharding unchanged — only assignment mechanism changed, no guard weakening. Isolated worktree (Rule 1); parallel-session ветки не тронуты (Rule 6); local commit only — NO push/PR/merge.
- **Status:** ADR-119 ACCEPTED (this branch, local). IL-NNN renumber-trap устранён; ручной il_ts re-mint на behind-PR больше не нужен. Files: ledger/build_ledger.py (modified), ledger/IL-SEQUENCE.json (new), docs/adr/ADR-119-stable-frozen-il-numbering.md (new), this shard.
- **Recommended next:** operator review diff; затем (отдельно, по слову оператора) push + PR + CI-gated squash-merge на agent/factory/ledger/stable-il-numbering. После merge — будущие behind-PR не требуют re-mint (стабильная нумерация). Parallel-session ветки не трогать.
- **Refs:** docs/adr/ADR-119-stable-frozen-il-numbering.md; ledger/build_ledger.py; ledger/IL-SEQUENCE.json; ADR-059 (sharded ledger), ADR-056 (ledger-coupling, unchanged), ADR-057; I-28.

### S-FAC-60 R0 hygiene — track guardian pre-push hook + ignore transient buffers (no behavior change)
- **Date:** 2026-06-23 · **Type:** repo hygiene; config/hook tracking + .gitignore; NO logic/PATTERN change, no protection/ledger-history mutation.
- **Decision:** (1) Bring `.githooks/pre-push` under version control (byte-identical to the already-tracked source-of-truth `scripts/pre-push-branch-name.sh`, sha1 `eece3be…`); (2) extend `.gitignore` with `.quarantine/` and `docs/incoming/`.
- **Instrukciya:** Close two audit findings without altering guardian behavior: host-drift risk (the active ADR-060 branch-naming mirror was untracked while its sibling `.githooks/pre-commit` is tracked) and accidental-staging risk (no ignore rule for transient buffers).
- **Basis (audit):** live shell audit @ mark-legion 2026-06-23 ~16:00 UTC. Finding 1: `.githooks/pre-push` executable + active (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`) but UNTRACKED — evo1/evo2 lacking the STDIN-refs root-cause fix could pass a bad branch (the exact bug the hook header documents). Finding 2: `.gitignore` had no `.quarantine/` / `docs/incoming/` entry.
- **Best-solution rationale:** source-of-truth `scripts/pre-push-branch-name.sh` is already tracked and `scripts/install-hooks.sh` copies it to `.githooks/pre-push`; repo policy already tracks `.githooks/` (`.githooks/pre-commit`). Tracking `.githooks/pre-push` (mode 100755, identical bytes) makes a fresh checkout carry the correct hook directly — eliminating drift — with zero behavior change. PATTERN `^agent/(central|right|factory)/[A-Za-z0-9]+/[a-z0-9._-]+$` unchanged; source of truth remains guardian.yml.
- **Change (minimal, no duplication):** +track `.githooks/pre-push`; +2 additive `.gitignore` lines (no reordering); +1 new ledger shard. No existing tracked file edited except additive `.gitignore`; no prior ledger entry mutated; `.quarantine/`/`docs/incoming/` CONTENTS never staged.
- **Canon compliance:** live-audit source of truth (not memory); best-solution; minimal-diff; append-only ledger (ADR-119 frozen IL via IL-SEQUENCE.json, max+1); branch ADR-060-compliant (`agent/factory/hygiene/r0-guardian-gitignore`); no S320 (S314, Ruff ≥0.12.0); hooks enabled (no `--no-verify`/`--admin`/bypass); STOP before merge for operator.
- **Coupling/append-only:** branch off origin/main@d2716e2; no prior entry renumbered/modified; single new shard.
- **Proof:** `build_ledger.py --check` exit 0; guardian-ledger / ledger-append-only / guardian-ledger-shards / guardian-branch-naming green (local); squash PR opened to main (merge-queue); operator performs merge.

### ADR-121 — Parallel-session destructive-action protection (RULE 7): no destructive ops on shared/foreign state; resilience + recovery contract; pre-commit guard
- **Decision:** Created **ADR-121** (PERMANENT canon, ACCEPTED) establishing **RULE 7** — a session MUST NEVER run a destructive op against shared or foreign-session state it did not create: no `rm -rf` on any repo checkout, no deleting/corrupting `.git` (shared OR a linked worktree's `.git/worktrees/` admin), no `git worktree remove`/`prune` of foreign worktrees, no force-removal/update of foreign branches (`branch -D`/`push --delete`/`update-ref -d`), no `chattr`/perm/ownership change on shared `.git`. Cleanup is limited to the session's OWN isolated worktree (ADR-120; `bx-session.sh --cleanup`). RULE 7 is a **stop-barrier** (invariant priority, with `safety-rules.md`); uncertain target ⇒ **fail-closed** (treat as foreign, do not destroy) + escalate.
- **Basis (incident, not invented):** 2026-06-24 the shared checkout `/home/mmber/banxe-architecture` + its `.git` were **deleted mid-session** (external/parallel-session event). Because all **12 linked worktrees** had `gitdir`→`.git/worktrees/`, the single deletion **cascade-orphaned every worktree at once**. **No commits lost** (origin intact); recovered via `git clone`, `main` now at `06fac53`. Root causes: (a) shared `.git` = single point of failure for all linked worktrees; (b) no canon banned destructive ops on shared/foreign state; (c) ADR-120 isolated commits but not the substrate.
- **Resilience (eliminate SPOF):** ADR-121 recommends **independent clone per session** (own `.git`, no shared substrate) so destruction cannot cascade; if the linked-worktree model is kept, the shared `.git` MUST be **operator-protected** (`chattr +i` / backup) and the single-point-of-failure is documented + accepted. Honest limit recorded: RULE 7 binds sessions + the commit-time hook but cannot stop an arbitrary out-of-process `rm` — hence operator-side `.git` protection is required, not optional, under linked worktrees.
- **Recovery contract:** origin = source of truth; no local-only state is canonical. On shared-checkout/`.git` loss → recover via `git clone` from origin. Exact steps captured in **`docs/runbooks/recover-shared-checkout.md`** (audit-first → re-clone → `install-hooks.sh` (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`) → operator `chattr +i .git` → re-establish worktrees via `bx-session.sh`/`git worktree add` off fresh `origin/main`).
- **Memory persistence ("fix it in memory"):** appended **Rule 7** (+ destructive-op ban + resilience + recovery pointer) to `.claude/rules/parallel-session-isolation.md` (after Rule 6) and added the incident + ADR-120/121 to its Anchors, so every future factory/agent session loads RULE 7 across sessions.
- **Enforcement (`.githooks/pre-commit`, extended, minimal-diff, no false-block):** (a) **BLOCK** any commit staging git-internal/worktree-admin paths (`^\.git/` or `*/worktrees/*`) — never a legitimate commit ⇒ zero false-positives; (b) **WARN non-blocking** when a staged **`*.sh`** ADDS a RULE 7 destructive pattern (`rm -rf` / `git worktree remove|prune` / `branch -D` / `push --delete` / `chattr … .git`) — scoped to shell-script added lines so it never false-blocks docs that merely *mention* the patterns (incl. ADR-121 + the runbook) nor normal commits.
- **Proof:** Incident facts above are the recovered state (main `06fac53`; 12 worktrees orphaned; re-clone). `bash -n .githooks/pre-commit` clean. Guard verified BOTH directions: path-guard fires on `.git/config` + `foo/worktrees/bar`, ignores normal paths; danger-regex matches `rm -rf` + `git worktree remove`, ignores `echo hello`. This commit's staged set (ADR-121.md, parallel-session-isolation.md, recover runbook, .githooks/pre-commit, shard, INSTRUCTION-LEDGER.md, IL-SEQUENCE.json) triggers **neither** block (no `.git/`//worktrees/ path) **nor** warn (no `*.sh` staged) — confirmed no self-block. Anti-dup (ADR-102): no prior `ADR-121*` file or refs existed. Append-only (ADR-059-A): ONE new tail shard at il_ts `2026-06-24T23:00:00Z` (strictly > fresh tree max `2026-06-24T22:30:00Z` after rebase onto main `9634eb3`); INSTRUCTION-LEDGER.md + IL-SEQUENCE.json regenerated via `python3 ledger/build_ledger.py`, `--check` exit 0. Isolated worktree off `origin/main 06fac53` (ADR-120); shared checkout NOT mutated; **RULE 7 self-honored** (no destructive op run against any foreign state during this task).
- **Status:** ADR-121 + RULE 7 = DONE (permanent canon + memory mirror + recovery runbook + pre-commit guard). Host-side operator action remains: `chattr +i` / backup the shared `.git` (the durable SPOF protection a hook cannot provide). DO NOT MERGE pending operator review.

### Race-proof IL allocation — merge-time freeze + guardian IL-collision gate (docs/governance plane)

- **Objective:** Eliminate the duplicate-IL defect where concurrent factory terminals double-claim a number (493/494/497/500/501), violating I-28 and forcing Claude Code to stop and ask. Make IL allocation race-proof so collisions are caught pre-merge and re-id is autonomous.
- **Live audit (source of truth, not memory):** origin/main@9be1662; `python ledger/build_ledger.py --check` OK FROM ROOT; IL-SEQUENCE max=506 → this = frozen max+1 = **IL-507** (ADR-119). Verified contiguous tail through 506, zero duplicate IL numbers on main after the three re-ids.
- **Root cause:** no atomic IL allocation across concurrent terminals. `build_ledger.py` assigns `max+1` correctly, and `--check` validates the branch against its OWN HEAD — but a behind-branch can pass `--check` while carrying a number already frozen on `main` for a different shard. The duplicate only fails to land because branch protection is `strict`; it still surfaces as an I-28 collision (the "factory keeps asking" regression).
- **Resolution of the three colliding PRs (no content change beyond the IL number; rebase + regenerate FROM ROOT; append-only verified each = 1 new key / 0 mutated / 0 removed):**
  - #744 M2.8 Roster-C gate-resolution: stale IL-497 (taken by e-capital #745) → re-id **IL-503** (also passed over 502 taken by a-kyb #752 mid-flight). MERGED → main@974955a.
  - #749 DUP-clone salvage manifest: stale IL-500 (taken by a-kyc #748) → re-id **IL-504**. MERGED → main@27da8b5.
  - #751 s-fac-65 traffic-light: stale IL-501 (taken by a-idv #750) → re-id **IL-505**. MERGED → main@9634eb3.
- **Guard mechanism (A + B, by engineering merit):**
  - **A — canon (merge-time freeze):** `.claude/rules/parallel-session-isolation.md` **Rule 8** + **ADR-119 Amendment 2026-06-24**: IL number is provisional until the branch is rebased onto current `origin/main` immediately before merge and `build_ledger.py` (FROM ROOT) re-assigns `max+1`; never hardcoded at creation; `strict` protection physically blocks a behind-branch from merging a stale number; concurrent ledger PRs serialized; a mismatch is an autonomous rebase signal, NOT an operator question.
  - **B — CI gate spec:** `docs/guardian/guardian-ledger-il-collision-gate.md` — `guardian-ledger` REJECTS any PR whose new `IL-SEQUENCE.json` value duplicates an existing-on-main number bound to a different shard key (C1), or whose asserted `[IL-NNN]` ≠ regenerated number (C2), emitting a deterministic rebase+regenerate remediation message.
- **Named-ordinal collision (same class):** this guard's own Rule was assigned **Rule 7** initially, but ADR-121 (PR #753) landed its Rule 7 (destructive-action protection) concurrently; per append-only canon the merged Rule 7 keeps the number and this guard re-id'd its rule **7 → 8** (and IL-506 → IL-507) — the same merge-time-freeze discipline applied to a named ordinal.
- **ADR-102 dedup:** searched ledger/canon for existing IL-allocation guard — none; Rule 1-7 cover branch/stash/commit isolation + destructive-op protection but not number-collision; this is the first merge-time-freeze rule. Companion to (not duplicate of) ADR-119 (numbering mechanism) and existing guardian-ledger jobs (history immutability). No file moved/deleted; all additive.
- **Perimeter / gates NOT crossed:** docs/governance plane only; no code execution path, no client funds, no production state, no process management (the race is fixed by merge-time freeze + guardian gate + strict protection, NOT by killing sessions); no cross-repo write; no renumber of any prior entry; signed commits; `--force-with-lease` only.
- **Coupling/append-only:** branch agent/factory/ledgerguard/il-allocation (off main@9be1662); frozen IL via ledger/IL-SEQUENCE.json (max+1); no prior key mutated (249..506 unchanged); `--check` exit 0 FROM ROOT.

### ADR-122 — Mapping Anthropic finance agent templates → BANXE factory (skills/connectors/subagents); NO fork, reference-only
- **Decision:** Created `docs/adr/ADR-122-anthropic-finance-templates-mapping.md` (ACCEPTED, concept_only) mapping the 10 Anthropic finance agent templates (2026-05-05; Pitch builder, Meeting preparer, Earnings reviewer, Model builder, Market researcher, Valuation reviewer, General ledger reconciler, Month-end closer, Statement auditor, KYC screener) onto the existing BANXE agent layer, and fixing the decision: **DO NOT fork `anthropics/financial-services`** — borrow ONLY the 3-layer reference pattern (skills + connectors + subagents) as a design checklist where a gap exists. No external code/plugin/template imported; gap-closure is future PROPOSED passports (I-27), not import.
- **3-layer pattern already native in BANXE:** skills = `docs/SKILLS-MATRIX.md` (10 skills bound 57/57); connectors = adapter passports (jube/watchman/yente, midaz_mcp, clickhouse_writer) + hexagonal `ports:`; subagents = orchestration tree (`.claude/rules/agents.md`: L1 orchestrator → L2 sub-agents) + `agents/souls/` (19) + `agents/swarms/` (3).
- **Mapping result (10 templates → BANXE agent/passport → gap):** PRESENT 3 — General ledger reconciler (`safeguarding_recon_governor` + `clickhouse_writer` + `midaz_mcp_agent`, CASS-15 recon), Statement auditor (`internal_audit_agent` + `safeguarding_audit_agent` + `reporting_agent`), KYC screener (full AML/KYC stack: `sanctions_check`/`watchman_adapter`/`yente_adapter`/`adverse_media_governor`/`aml_orchestrator`/`banxe_aml_orchestrator`/`tx_monitor`/`crypto_aml`/`jube_adapter`/`case_management_agent`). PARTIAL 5 — Earnings reviewer (`cfo_orchestration_agent`+`reporting_agent`), Model builder (`treasury_alm_agent`+`ml_pipeline_agent`), Market researcher (MiroFish research swarm + `experiment_copilot_agent`), Valuation reviewer (`risk_oversight_agent`), Month-end closer (`cfo_orchestration_agent`+`reporting_agent`+`safeguarding_recon_governor`). GAP 2 — Pitch builder + Meeting preparer (front-office analyst agents BANXE does not have; dept-head stubs only). The compliance core matches the strongest external templates; the front-office/analyst templates are the gaps.
- **No-fork rationale (ADR-102):** BANXE already implements the 3-layer pattern on its own governed canon; forking `anthropics/financial-services` would duplicate an externally-governed agent set, cross the ADR-117 perimeter, and bypass passport/skill governance (I-27/I-28).
